Can you please tell us what was General Gvero's relationship with President Karadzic? Their personal relationship between General Gvero and President Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I could say it in the briefest possible terms, it was bad overall, with quite frequent verbal disagreements and plenty of dislike. Some parts of the leadership of the ruling party, for the most part officers of the former Yugoslav People's Army, and particularly General Gvero, because of his previous duties, believed that he was a throw-back from the past and somebody who was a proponent of brotherhood and unity and other values from the previous system.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did President Karadzic make any demands of General Gvero and the Main Staff regarding their status?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were a number of demands. First of all, there were requests -- actually, not requests, orders that he should not appear in the public information media. Then that he should be replaced and pensioned off. And this was something that was explicitly stated twice: Once at a session of the People's Assembly of Republika Srpska in Sanski Most; and for the second time at a session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us the Assembly of Republika Srpska was held where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the first assembly session that I meant was in Sanski Most. And the second one was in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the end of 1992, and we talked about it. Are you aware that in 1993 President Karadzic scheduled a meeting regarding the replacement of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I don't know whether this was in the form of a meeting, but I know that in 1993 the initiative came from the president of the republic to replace the commander of the Main Staff, Ratko Mladic, and then at least one more time there could have been another request before that, but I remember this one very well because it came after the fall of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina and the fall of the -- part of the area of Republika Srpska, in the western part of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I consult with the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can consult with -- not with the witness but with your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My client, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, but at non-audible volume. Should that be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to look at page 7 of this same document in the English version and page 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an interview with General Mladic. You were asked about the six strategic goals from his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to look at the right-hand upper column in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should enlarge it further. Yes, only focus on the right column.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's the middle one. We have the right one, yeah. And it's the last paragraph in English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Mladic compares the JNA and the Army of Republika Srpska, but I'm not going to read the whole thing. But he says about the Army of Republika Srpska: "This is a people's army and a people's army cannot be defeated. What is the source of the difference in the effectiveness and organisation of these two armies? I would say that, apart from our army having a clearer strategic goal, it is here to protect its own people. The people are here and, just like its people, it has no place to retreat." Does that correspond to what you understood to be the strategic goals of the fight of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at P6646.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your document from November 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to look at page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 12, you were asked about the masking of offensive activities and that the public was not informed about it. This was concealed from the public and they were misinformed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go back to page 1, item 1 of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 1 states: "In the present context, point out the intensification of Muslim offensive operations, their commitment to the war option, and the hypocritical behaviour of the Croatian side in the civil war on the territory of the former B and H." At that time, in late 1994 thus, was this a misrepresentation of the reality or was this an instruction about reporting truthfully; namely, at that time, were there intensive Muslim offences ongoing at that time and was their commitment to the war option clear?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and precisely for this reason. This instruction was written for the purposes of informing the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 5 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we need to look at page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- where it states in paragraph 5: "Point out the international community's double standards towards the sides in the conflict ..." Is this something that was misinformation or did it correspond to the actual situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was realistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber - and I checked with my colleagues - is puzzled by your questions. Because number 1 is about the other parties' operations, whereas paragraph 12 is about Serb operations, and there was no suggestion, as far as I understand, that in every respect the instructions were always to -- to not tell the truth on all things but specifically on offensive Serbian operations after having masked them at a later stage to present them as defensive. That is totally unrelated, as far as the Chamber understands, with the matters you're raising now in your questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If the Prosecution can stipulate that the rest of this information is truthful --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's not about -- these are instructions. What the Prosecution did is to put to the witness that instruction number 12 was an instruction to give false information. They did not touch upon the other instructions, whether that would be -- and so therefore, there's no -- of course, if you want to stipulate, Mr. Traldi, you're free to do that. But it is unrelated and there was no suggestion that all the other instructions would lead to untruthful information. That was not suggested in any way. Only 12 did. Let's leave it to that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the whole document was introduced --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said let's leave it to that, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to continue with this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, not saying you can't continue with the document, but please put questions which are related to what was dealt with in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sokanovic, according to you, the other items in this document, were they intended to misinform the public or was the intention to inform the public properly?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intention was to properly inform the public, and this guidance was drafted as a supplement to the instruction about informing the public, and it had to do with the actual or current political and military situation in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2 now in B/C/S. Let us look at paragraphs 9 and 12 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there an order issued by the president of the republic, Mr. Sokanovic, about a ban on providing information in the media about the movements, formation names, and insignia of VRS units?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Revealing offensive activities, would that mean disclosing a military secret?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that was already indicated in previous documents, how detrimental such things would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What would you say? What was your intention? In paragraph 12, were you implementing paragraph 9?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Without leading, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's hard to not lead at least a bit and stay in a time-frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You should properly examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1994 in November, did the Army of Republika Srpska capture anything on the ground?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was carrying out offensive activities in 1994 in November when this information was being sent, when this paper was being sent?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Offensive activities were carried out by the so-called Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Croatian Democratic Council, and in that period, that is to say, just before this, they took about 250 square kilometres of territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just look at P6915 now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just say the number, please, again, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's P6915. [Interpretation] We had the same problem with calling up this document when my colleague Mr. Traldi was calling it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we have a document of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska before us. It's dated the 24th of April, 1993. The name of General Manojlo Milovanovic is typewritten at the bottom of the document. Lists are being required of different POWs and detained civilians. Do you know that in the territory of Republika Srpska there were civilian prisons?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were prisons under the control of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked a lot about prisons and camps. Apart from that visit a few days after you arrived in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina yet again from Serbia, did you have any duties that had to do with prisons and camps in territory that was under VRS control?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have any such duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any duties related to the interrogation of detained persons, or was this within somebody else's purview?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this does not belong to the sector for morale and religious affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the witness repeatedly told us this in response to the questions put by Mr. Traldi, so to that extent it's repetitious and it's not -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I have one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sokanovic, just this. Do you know which prisoners General Milovanovic was asking for through this document that is before us?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I said I think a moment ago that this was the first time I'm seeing this document. Now I managed to look at it a bit more, and I see that information is being requested about prisoners of war, Serbs from the territory of Republika Srpska that are in the prisons of the Republic of Croatia and Herceg-Bosna and Serb and Montenegrins from the territory of the former SRBiH and national minorities from the territory of Yugoslavia that are in the prisons of the Republic of Croatia and Herceg-Bosna but were members of the JNA, then civilians who are in prisons in the Republic of Croatia and Herceg-Bosna, then civilians from the territory of the former BiH that are in the villages and towns of the Republic of Croatia and Herceg-Bosna, then captured Croatian civilians from the territory of the Republic of Croatia and Herceg-Bosna who are in prisons of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. You read that from the document. But do you know which prisons General Milovanovic was referring to? Did you talk to him about that? Do you have any personal knowledge about this activity?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's just look at a document briefly, P7395.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the Command of the 1st Zvornik Brigade. It's signed by Colonel Vinko Pandurevic. You were asked what the word "poturice" meant. In the first paragraph, from the very beginning, it says: "The moment has come when the issue of liberating the Serb lands from Poturice will finally be resolved in this area by a resolute and successful action of our forces. Obviously, the enemy cannot be allowed to bring into question the fate of the Serb people in this area anymore by countless violations of truces signed to date." Who is it that is violating the truces? The soldiers of the other side or civilians?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers, of course. How could civilians do that? They do not have the force to do that, and they are not signatories.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now read the second part that was read out to you, the beginning of the second page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's pretty condensed in English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The part that was quoted was the lower part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's beginning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Adequate response..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- at the beginning of the first page and it goes onto the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what was put to you: "The adequate response of our forces meant that we realised that there would be no peace and security in Semberija and Donja Podrinje until the Poturice were completely defeated and driven out of this area in the fight for a single Serb territory. Our response to the enemy offensive enemy combat operations have been going on for one month in our brigade's zone of responsibility." When you read this in context, how would you understand the word "poturice" here? Does it refer to Muslim civilians --

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- or their military forces?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is meant here is military forces. Because it is against them that the offensive was taking place or, rather, it was a response to their offensive, and it says in the next sentence that this is a responses to their offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let us go back to page 1 of this version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 11 in B/C/S. And the last third -- the fifth line from the bottom of the first paragraph in the English version. It starts with the word: "And ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is what it says. I quote: "And so the Poturice launched an all-out offensive against Majevica and Vlasic and other strategic features and areas in Republika Srpska." So this part, does it have to do with the military or civilians?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is only military forces that can launch an offensive. So it is the army, not civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sokanovic. That is all we had. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, do you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I do. Less than ten minutes. I'll be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we have one translation issue, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's first hear that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this part -- I was just warned by my colleague Ivetic that in this part it says "Muslims" not "poturice." So it was actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where is that in?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the right page in both B/C/S and English? Because the word "poturice" is mentioned several times in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we still on page 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which line in B/C/S? To be compared with which line in ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we have to -- we stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You stand corrected. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Mr. Traldi. Further cross-examination by Mr. Traldi:

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stay on this document, sir. Second paragraph, Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic or in Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic's document, we read: "We must dash for all time their hope of creating a Muslimanija extending to the Drina and the Sava and make it possible for our people to return to their centuries-old homes, Vitinice, Rastosnice, and other Serbian places in the area."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, can we have 65 ter 02559, page 296. In the B/C/S. 296 in the B/C/S. If we go to line 28, we see Vitinice. And if we turn to the next page for the 1991 numbers, we see on the left side the columns and the headings total persons, Croats, Muslims, Serbs. If we scroll down to line 28, we see that before the war Vitinice was a village comprised of 2900 [Realtime transcript read in error "2800"] Muslims, about 200 Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the homes that Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic is saying "our people should be able to return to," those are homes that at the beginning of the war were inhabited by Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time I'm seeing this, so it's hard for me to give any comment. But again, I'm saying it would be best to ask Mr. Pandurevic what it was that he meant. But homes do not date back only to the Second World War. There are some that date back to before that, that are older than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just a correction for the transcript. In line 16 of page 58, Mr. Traldi said "2900" Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what you said just now, are you agreeing with Colonel Pandurevic that it would appropriate for villages that had been Serb at the Second World War, before the Second World War, even older than that, to be made Serbian again as a result of operations conducted in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree. I think - and that's what I've been explaining all along - that the territory of Republika Srpska should not be populated by the Serb people only, and the territory that would be under the political leadership of the Croat people should not be populated by Croats only. And the same goes for the third sides. And that is not possible even if somebody wanted to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I won't tender this. I assume my colleague agrees that I've correctly recited the pre-war census figures for this village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, no problem as far as that is concerned? That's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic asked you about your order in November 1994 to maximally mask offensive activities and present them at their advanced stages as defensive or as counterattacks. First, did I correctly understand your answer that in giving that instruction you understood yourself to be implementing an order from the supreme commander, President Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it's not clear to me which instruction you -- you mean, because very different instructions would come from the president of the republic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, you issued an instruction to mask offensive activities maximally, you issued an instruction to present them at the advanced stages as counter-attacks or -- part of the natural right to self-defence. On re-direct, you said you had believed yourself to have been implementing point 9 in the same document, an order from Karadzic about military secrets. So I want you to confirm now that in ordering the offensive activities to be masked maximally, presented as defence, you were implementing an order from Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, first of all, I cannot order anybody. I don't have that authority. I could give guidance or instructions. The document refers to a document by the president of the republic, Mr. Karadzic, and I assume that it was drafted on the basis of what was written in that order. As for the masking, masking is one of the measures used to protect secret data about the deployment, size, strength, intentions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was this what you asked, Mr. Traldi? The second part not. You have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Finally, sir, Mr. Lukic asked you about the relationship between President Karadzic and General Mladic and President Karadzic and General Gvero. Those generals kept their positions on the Main Staff throughout the war; right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, could we have P3076, page 18 in English and 13 in B/C/S. As it comes up, I'll remind you of the article we saw on cross-examination where President Karadzic noted the duty of the Serbian people to avoid the danger of extermination and create a state in which there will be none of its enemies. Now, we need page 18 in the English. This is part of the transcript of the 37th Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly. General Mladic is speaking, and he says at the end of this long paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first give an opportunity to the witness to find it and to be able to follow your reading, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you then slowly read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The end of this long paragraph, we read General Mladic say: "The next thing is that this is our historical chance to create a state. Not any kind of state, but an all-Serbian state of a round shape with access to the sea and horogravske and horografske facilities and as little enemies as possible, those who could be our potential enemies and raise against us again in a few years." Sir, what I'm putting to you is regardless of any temporary disagreements that you may have mentioned on re-direct, when it came to what mattered, the purpose of the war, President Karadzic and General Mladic were in such lockstep that they described that purpose in almost the same terms. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO SOKANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that this in case because then I would need to read the entire speech. Because one sentence, even if it's in agreement with the other person, in this case the president of the republic, does not mean that there wasn't a conflict between them. I stand by my words that there were serious clashes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Sokanovic, this concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, questions put to you by the Defence, by the Prosecution, by the Bench. I wish you a safe return home again. You play follow the usher. Mr. Mladic, I again and again have to emphasise that you should not speak aloud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, may I take it that you'll examine the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, and he should be in stand by in the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what would you prefer, to take the break now so that to -- and then that we would resume at 1.30 so that you have an uninterrupted 45 minutes, or would you like to start for five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think the first option is more agreeable so we have an uninterrupted ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take the break first and we'll resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the next witness to be escorted in the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, I understand that the Defence has problems with extended sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Although I said -- yes, Your Honour. Although I said at the beginning that we do not have a problem, I was reminded that we have scheduled a lot of meetings before we depart for our field trip. We travel on Saturday to investigate Tomasica, and we have to have really many meetings on Thursday and Friday already scheduled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I had as well. I moved them in order to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not have where to move them. We will be absent for a month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Lukic. I do understand that your schedule is so busy that's not even a way to move for two hours. I leave it to that at the time being. The parties are invited to further discuss whether they can fit the examination of the remaining witnesses of this week within an agreed time schedule. Again, the Chamber is available for extended sessions on Thursday. If not, then, of course, you should take measures so as to not leave a witness here for four weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What we wanted to inquire with the Prosecution, probably that should be a topic of our conversation, is we might send one witness back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that should be the last-resort solution but finally it might come to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it's not very polite to continue with our conversation when you enter the courtroom. Mr. Pajic, I presume. Mr. Pajic, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you -- yes. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you give a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, please be seated. You'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You find Mr. Ivetic to your left, standing. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can first my colleague Mr. Lukic be excused. He has to attend to something and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one of his meetings perhaps. Yes, you are excused, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Pajic. I would ask you to state your full name so that we can have it properly entered into the trial record.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to greet all those present in the courtroom. I am Velo Pajic. I come from Rogatica, Republika Srpska, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, have you testified previously at this Tribunal as a witness?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, in November 2008 in the Popovic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I note that in the summary provided the witness was born in the 11th century; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's definitely an error. Without having it in front of me, but I'm sure it's an error. I will address that with the witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 28th of July, 1960, in Rogatica, the then-Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, can you briefly outline for us the educational institutions that you attended, both civilian and military in nature?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I completed elementary school in 1975 in Borike near Rogatica, and then I completed the secondary military school of the land forces in Belgrade, the communications section of that school.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And upon completion of your education, did you become a member of the military?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Upon completion of my schooling, I joined the Yugoslav People's Army, and my rank was sergeant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What were your total years of service within the military during your career?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I spent the period from 1979, from the 18 -- until the 18th of May, 1992 in the Yugoslav army, not counting the years of my schooling. That was the period I spent in the Yugoslav People's Army. Then I was in the Army of Republika Srpska from the 18th of May, 1992, until the 1st of April, 1995. Then I spent the rest of my time until retirement in the Podgorica garrison --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter kindly asks the witness to repeat the other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the date when you stopped serving in the Army of Republika Srpska? I believe that is what is needed.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Until the 1st of April, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The date when you left the Army of Republika Srpska. Was that 2002 or some other date?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the highest rank that you attained prior to your retirement?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The highest rank was captain. I was captain when I retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how did your service in the VRS end?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: From the 18th of May, 1992, until the 1st of April, 2002, I served in the 67th Communications Regiment of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska performing the duties of commander of the 2nd Platoon of the frequency-carrying devices of the 4th Communications Garrison. I served in the special purpose facility Goljak 1, or G-1 for short.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In April of 2002 when you left the VRS, where did you go? You indicated that you were in a garrison in Podgorica. Could you repeat where you went and where you retired?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Once I completed my term in the Army of Republika Srpska, on the 1st of April, 2002, I went to the Podgorica garrison as commander of a radio-relay node which was located in the Lofcin [phoen] facility near Podgorica, and then on the 31st of December 2003 I was relieved of that post.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And within which armed forces was that?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The Army of Yugoslavia, and then it was renamed as the Army of Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to take you back to the beginning of 1992 when tensions broke out in Sarajevo. To what post or position were you assigned within the JNA at that time?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Once I completed military school, I went to work at the garrison in Sarajevo military post 1519. And then I worked at the Secretariat for National Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, [Interpretation] could you please speak more slowly so that the interpreters could catch what are you actually saying.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Very well. So after 1985 I was sent to Konjic where special purpose facilities were located, which were maintained by my unit, the one from military post 1519, where I remained until 1992, the 9th of May, 1992. The special purpose facilities, if I may clarify, were intended for the command and control of the armed forces of the former SFRY in war time by the Presidency, so it was the facility -- DILJ0 was the war time command post of the former Yugoslavia. At the time, the -- a facility D-1 was also there. It was a radio-relay station which was linked with D-0, and the distance between them was 1.5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [In English] And as far as D-0 is concerned, what kind of military structure or building was that?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I already said that these were special purpose underground facilities where there were rooms located for control and command, where the communications centre was situated, and the engine and electrical facilities for the operation of the facility in special circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what, sir, were your precise duties within the special purposes facility DILJ0 or D-0 at Konjic?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the section. My task was to maintain the telephone devices and the main frequency-carrying devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was feature D-0 operational or functional prior to the outbreak of war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: D-0 was operational. I think it began to work in Trnovo and it was first launched in 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. How long in 1992 did you stay at that post, the feature D-0, at the Konjic garrison?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: In 1992, sometime in early 1992, I was transferred to the T-1 facility because I completed higher school and I received the rank of second-lieutenant. So I'm talking about the D-1 facility, which is 1 kilometre or 1.5 kilometres away. I was the commander of that facility. I stayed there until 9th of May, 1992. Let me just remind you that D-0, D-1, and T-1 were facilities which were encircled by the Croat-Muslim forces. The encirclement lasted sometime from February until the 9th of May when we managed to pull out from the encirclement. We had to leave that area on foot. There were about 38 of us senior officers, and we were joined on the way by civilians, women, children, and then we reached another sector. So I repeat again: We passed through the lines of the enemy forces, of the KOS forces and the Green Berets, and we came to the Bijelasnica mountain, from where we were transferred to the command of the 398th Brigade by choppers in the evening on the 9th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: During the time-period that were encircled by these forces from February until the 9th of May, how did you and others that were at that location survive in terms of supplies and food and the like?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: During the last month, it was very difficult. Let me just remind you that those facilities were being supplied with food for the next six months. So this happened in November. Since this was already May, it meant we were running low on food, and there were many more of us than during peacetime periods so that we were forced to eat mouldy crackers and there were some other dry foods that we had to eat, just basic foodstuffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You indicated that eventually the -- you were transferred by choppers to the command of the 398th Brigade. Could you tell us in what city that brigade command is located where you were transferred by helicopters?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The brigade command. Earlier there were three communication regiments, later this 398th Brigade was formed. Its seat was in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the JNA personnel that had been under encirclement with you at the facility T-1 who were withdrawn to Belgrade by helicopters, what was the ethnicity of those personnel?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: At that time all the ethnic groups were represented there. There were ethnic Croat, ethnic Muslims. We had ethnic Albanians there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: That is to say, we all got out of there together, including these civilians that joined us. They were taken to the garrison in Belgrade, all of that by helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I stayed in Belgrade from the 9th of May in the evening until the 18th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where did you go after the 18th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: After that day, I was transferred in a service vehicle to Han Pijesak, the area of Crna Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And just to complete the circle, to which unit did you belong at the time that you were in Crna Rijeka after the 18th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The unit where I served in Crna Rijeka from the 18th of May onwards was the 67th Communications Regiment of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, the company for communications for garrison communications, the commander of the 2nd Battalion for frequency-carrying devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as commander of this 2nd Platoon within the 67th Communications Regiment, can you tell us what the strength in terms of manpower of that platoon was in reality when you became its commander?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: It was just me on my own, one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did the manpower of that platoon change during the duration of the war and the duration of your time at Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Actually, yes, later. I got this soldier who was doing his military service all the time, so basically it was I and that soldier who were there, in that platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, what was the manpower strength of that platoon supposed to be per establishment protocol?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: According to establishment, about 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you already told us earlier that you were at the Goljak 1 feature. Could you tell us what is the Goljak 1 feature? What kind of a structure or installation is it?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Goljak 1, abbreviated as G-1, was a special purposes facility. They were called D and M and G features, and they were envisaged for command and control in wartime conditions; specifically, G was envisaged as the command post in wartime of the then-7th Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And which command post of the 7th Army of the former SFRY forces was this feature Goljak 1 intended to be?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Goljak was in Han Pijesak in the area of Crna Rijeka. That's about 8 kilometres away from Han Pijesak. And the command post of the 7th Army was in Zlatiste in Sarajevo - the war time command post, I repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What were your precise duties within this position as commander of the 2nd Platoon within the 67th Communications Regiment?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: My duties were to establish and maintain radio relay and wire communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how long did you spend working at this same physical location at that same position?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Ten years. Or, rather, nine years, ten months, approximately. The 18th of May, 1992, until the 1st of July, 2002. Almost ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did your duty post or position title ever change?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1999, I became commander of the G features. I'm saying G features because there was also G-2 and G-3; in addition to G-1, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were these additional features G-2 and G-3 outfitted and operational during the time-period of the war; that is to say, from 1993 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: G-2 was partly equipped; that is to say, there were certain premises but the communications were not installed. Also, the bathroom facilities did not function. And G-3, the building was just set up but it was not properly outfitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to take a look together at a Prosecution exhibit, P6848 in e-court. Sir, when that comes up on your monitor, I'll ask you first if you recognise what is depicted in that picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could perhaps have just one copy and enlarge it, that might assist us all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise what is depicted in this picture?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the overground building of G-1, and it was called Vila Javor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now you say this is the overground building of G-1. Where in relation to this building that we have on our screen is the entrance to the underground facility of G-1?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: This facility was used not only in this case but in all other such cases. It was just used as a disguise for entering the underground facility. You enter through this door or through the garage door, and then you would go further on into the underground facility, G-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I would like to ask you what kind of communications systems were available to the Main Staff of the VRS at Crna Rijeka at G-1?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: In G-1, there was an automatic telephone exchange that was called OM 60/250, automatic three digit numbers. And then there was also an exchange table, as we called it, for communication between direct and automatic connections. Then there was also a room where there were telephones, or rather frequency-carrying devices. Then there was a room where telegraphs were, teleprinters, and also the encryption station. Teleprinter encryption station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to be clear, where was the command of the Main Staff of the VRS located at Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The command of the Main Staff was a kilometre away from this Vila Javor facility. It was in prefabricated buildings about 1 kilometre away from this facility, and the commander of the Main Staff, General Mladic, was in Vila Javor, that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What kinds of communications technology were available to the Main Staff during the war to communicate with those outside of Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: There was a communications system and these were wire communications, radio communications, and radio-relay communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to first focus on radio-relay communications, the last one you mentioned. Could you briefly explain for us how those functioned and -- to describe the difference between radio-relay communications and radio communications which was the second of the items that you identified?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Radio-relay communications were used for transmitting speech and written material through wireless telecommunications, through electromagnetic waves that were modulated at higher frequencies, and through antennae they were transmitted to the other side. In order -- I mean, I a radio relay devices, I mean, the ones that we had at the time in that period were as follows: RRU-800, FM-200, SNC-1306B, and RRU-1. Those were the types that we had, and there had to be other equipment plugged into that. Now, it depends on whether these were protected or unprotected communications.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness start again now with the specific communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The interpreters could not follow the last part of your answer. Could you please repeat the last part after you identified RRU-1. And then you said that the difference in relation to other equipment is, and then could you please complete what it was that you were trying to say.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I listed the types of equipment. Once again --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you should really slow down. Otherwise, parts of your words will be lost. I leave it in your hands, Mr. Ivetic, where to resume.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you could resume speaking slowly. You had just finished talking about the RRU-1 and said it depended on equipment that could be attached to all these RRU devices, whether they were protected communications or ... And that is where we lost the translation, so if could you please take up your answer from approximately there and repeat it, this time more slowly, so that the interpreters can catch every word.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Very well. So there were two types of radio-relay communications. There was one type that were protected and the other type that were unprotected. Protected radio-relay communications were between radio-relay stations, and this also goes for unprotected ones. It was 50 kilometres. In order for protected communication to be communicated, we need FM-200, then antennae, then AND 310, and of course a generator. In order to have unprotected communication, analogous, we also need two radio-relay communication stations 50 kilometres away. We need a proper signal; that is to say, an excellent signal that can guarantee communication. Everything else could be a problem for relaying written communication and speech. For that, we would need RRU-800, SNC-1306B, 12K and V120. Again, I'm saying that their frequency for RRU-800 and for FM-200 is from 610 to 960 megahertz. For SNC, it is a higher frequency, 4.400 to 4.600 megahertz and from 4.800 to 5.000 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the radio-relay communications between the Main Staff and subordinated units, were those of the -- of the encrypted and protected or of the open type or unprotected type that you have described?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Between the Main Staff and subordinated units, it went without saying; that is to say, the logistic command post, the staff units of the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps, then the Eastern Bosnia Corps, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, the Presidency, the Army of Yugoslavia, we had both. That is to say, we had protected and unprotected types of radio-relay communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You've listed several, and I'm looking at the transcript, what about the radio-relay communications between the Main Staff and the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I forgot to mention that. There was also radio-relay communication with -- along two relay routes. One was protected and the other one was unprotected. This one, the unprotected one, was RRU-800, RM4, where the frequency distribution of channels 3- to 800 kilohertz, and the protected one functioned, and the number was 0674, and the previous one was 0607.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now between the unprotected and the protected radio-relay routes between the Main Staff and the Drina Corps, for what type of communications was each used during the war?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The secured route, 0674, which after the change, because of the same direction on the neighbouring facility was changed to 0658, operated eight protected channels. This was done on the relay device FM-200. Multi-challenge device with a time distribution or frequency binary or secured transfer of the channel. These eight channels were connected directly to channels to an intercom or a telephone exchange on the other side. The commander of the Main Staff of the Drina Corps. The second channel was the operations centre of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, the operations centre of the Drina Corps. The third channel was the exchange of the Main Staff of the RS, the exchange of the Drina Corps. And then the fourth channel was used for an automatic telephone number from the existing exchange, which was at the G-1 facility, 332, that was the phone number. The telegraph had an alternative. The telegraph communications were -- meaning the transfer of written information, since they were secured, encrypted, where the data was processed, they could be transferred either through the analog or the digital system. So if one route was cut, we had an alternate route where this could function. So let me go back to these encrypted telegrams. They were protected on the digital and the analogue route, and all of that was processed in the range from 600 to 900 megahertz. Now, I'm talking about the FM-200 and the RRU-800 devices.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I need one minute before we adjourn so, therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's stop here then. Witness, we'll adjourn for the day soon. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.30 in this same courtroom. Before you leave, I instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or whether it's testimony still to be given tomorrow or even the day after tomorrow. If that is clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber would like to hear from the parties if there's any conclusion as far as scheduling for this week is concerned, because we were about, on the basis of what -- of the information provided by the Defence, to start organising an extended session for Thursday, but that seems to be uncertain by now. Therefore, as soon as the parties have agreed or have concluded their discussions on the matter, the Chamber would like to be informed without delay. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 20th of May, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of May, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
